# Ident in unsynn - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/unsynn/^0.3/struct.Ident.html

`pub struct Ident { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

A word of Rust code, which may be a keyword or legal variable name.

An identifier consists of at least one Unicode code point, the first of which has the XID_Start property and the rest of which have the XID_Continue property.

- The empty string is not an identifier. Use `Option<Ident>`.
- A lifetime is not an identifier. Use `syn::Lifetime`instead.

An identifier constructed with `Ident::new` is permitted to be a Rust
keyword, though parsing one through its [ Parse](https://docs.rs/syn/2.0/syn/parse/trait.Parse.html) implementation rejects
Rust keywords. Use

`input.call(Ident::parse_any)` when parsing to match the
behaviour of `Ident::new`.[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

A new ident can be created from a string using the `Ident::new` function.
A span must be provided explicitly which governs the name resolution
behavior of the resulting identifier.

```
use proc_macro2::{Ident, Span};
fn main() {
    let call_ident = Ident::new("calligraphy", Span::call_site());
    println!("{}", call_ident);
}
```
An ident can be interpolated into a token stream using the `quote!` macro.

```
use proc_macro2::{Ident, Span};
use quote::quote;
fn main() {
    let ident = Ident::new("demo", Span::call_site());
    // Create a variable binding whose name is this ident.
    let expanded = quote! { let #ident = 10; };
    // Create a variable binding with a slightly different name.
    let temp_ident = Ident::new(&format!("new_{}", ident), Span::call_site());
    let expanded = quote! { let #temp_ident = 10; };
}
```
A string representation of the ident is available through the `to_string()`
method.

```
// Examine the ident as a string.
let ident_string = ident.to_string();
if ident_string.len() > 60 {
    println!("Very long identifier: {}", ident_string)
}
```
## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

Creates a new `Ident` with the given `string` as well as the specified
`span`.

The `string` argument must be a valid identifier permitted by the
language, otherwise the function will panic.

Note that `span`, currently in rustc, configures the hygiene information
for this identifier.

As of this time `Span::call_site()` explicitly opts-in to “call-site”
hygiene meaning that identifiers created with this span will be resolved
as if they were written directly at the location of the macro call, and
other code at the macro call site will be able to refer to them as well.

Later spans like `Span::def_site()` will allow to opt-in to
“definition-site” hygiene meaning that identifiers created with this
span will be resolved at the location of the macro definition and other
code at the macro call site will not be able to refer to them.

Due to the current importance of hygiene this constructor, unlike other
tokens, requires a `Span` to be specified at construction.

[§](https://docs.rs#panics)Panics

Panics if the input string is neither a keyword nor a legal variable
name. If you are not sure whether the string contains an identifier and
need to handle an error case, use
`syn::parse_str``::<Ident>`
rather than `Ident::new`.

Same as `Ident::new`, but creates a raw identifier (`r#ident`). The
`string` argument must be a valid identifier permitted by the language
(including keywords, e.g. `fn`). Keywords which are usable in path
segments (e.g. `self`, `super`) are not supported, and will cause a
panic.

# Literal in unsynn - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/unsynn/^0.3/struct.Literal.html

`pub struct Literal { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

A literal string (`"hello"`), byte string (`b"hello"`), character (`'a'`),
byte character (`b'a'`), an integer or floating point number with or without
a suffix (`1`, `1u8`, `2.3`, `2.3f32`).

Boolean literals like `true` and `false` do not belong here, they are
`Ident`s.

## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

[Source](https://docs.rs/proc-macro2/1.0.103/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/proc_macro2/lib.rs.html#1130-1143)#### pub fn [u8_suffixed](https://docs.rs#method.u8_suffixed)(n: [u8](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u8.html)) -> [Literal](https://docs.rs/struct.Literal.html)

[Source](https://docs.rs/proc-macro2/1.0.103/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/proc_macro2/lib.rs.html#1130-1143)

#### pub fn [u8_suffixed](https://docs.rs#method.u8_suffixed)(n: [u8](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u8.html)) -> [Literal](https://docs.rs/struct.Literal.html)

Creates a new suffixed integer literal with the specified value.

This function will create an integer like `1u32` where the integer
value specified is the first part of the token and the integral is
also suffixed at the end. Literals created from negative numbers may
not survive roundtrips through `TokenStream` or strings and may be

Creates a new unsuffixed integer literal with the specified value.

This function will create an integer like `1` where the integer
value specified is the first part of the token. No suffix is
specified on this token, meaning that invocations like
`Literal::i8_unsuffixed(1)` are equivalent to
`Literal::u32_unsuffixed(1)`. Literals created from negative numbers
may not survive roundtrips through `TokenStream` or strings and may
be broken into two tokens (`-` and positive literal).

Literals created through this method have the `Span::call_site()`
span by default, which can be configured with the `set_span` method
below.

# Repeats in unsynn - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/unsynn/^0.3/type.Repeats.html

`pub type Repeats<const MIN: `[usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html), const MAX: [usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html), T, D = [Nothing](https://docs.rs/struct.Nothing.html), P = [Optional](https://docs.rs/TrailingDelimiter/struct.Optional.html)> = [DelimitedVec](https://docs.rs/struct.DelimitedVec.html)<T, D, P, MIN, MAX>;## Expand description

`DelimitedVec<T,D>` with a minimum and maximum (inclusive) number of elements at first
without defaults.  Parsing will succeed when at least the minimum number of elements is
reached and stop at the maximum number.  The delimiter `D` defaults to [ Nothing](https://docs.rs/struct.Nothing.html) to
parse sequences which don’t have delimiters.

# Punct in unsynn - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/unsynn/^0.3/struct.Punct.html

`pub struct Punct { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

A `Punct` is a single punctuation character like `+`, `-` or `#`.

Multicharacter operators like `+=` are represented as two instances of
`Punct` with different forms of `Spacing` returned.

## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

Creates a new `Punct` from the given character and spacing.

The `ch` argument must be a valid punctuation character permitted by the
language, otherwise the function will panic.

The returned `Punct` will have the default span of `Span::call_site()`
which can be further configured with the `set_span` method below.

Returns the spacing of this punctuation character, indicating whether
it’s immediately followed by another `Punct` in the token stream, so
they can potentially be combined into a multicharacter operator
(`Joint`), or it’s followed by some other token or whitespace (`Alone`)
so the operator has certainly ended.

# Skip in unsynn - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/unsynn/^0.3/struct.Skip.html

`pub struct Skip<T>(/* private fields */);`## Expand description

Skips over expected tokens. Will parse and consume the tokens but not store them.
Consequently the `ToTokens` implementations will not output any tokens.

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

```
let mut token_iter = "ident,".to_token_iter();
let _ = Skip::<Cons<Ident, Comma>>::parse_all(&mut token_iter).unwrap();
```

# Span in unsynn - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/unsynn/^0.3/struct.Span.html

`pub struct Span { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

`unsynn` reexports the entities from `proc_macro2` it implements `Parse` and `ToTokens` for.
A region of source code, along with macro expansion information.

## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

The span of the invocation of the current procedural macro.

Identifiers created with this span will be resolved as if they were written directly at the macro call location (call-site hygiene) and other code at the macro call site will be able to refer to them as well.

[Source](https://docs.rs/proc-macro2/1.0.103/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/proc_macro2/lib.rs.html#390)#### pub fn [mixed_site](https://docs.rs#method.mixed_site)() -> [Span](https://docs.rs/struct.Span.html)

[Source](https://docs.rs/proc-macro2/1.0.103/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/proc_macro2/lib.rs.html#390)

#### pub fn [mixed_site](https://docs.rs#method.mixed_site)() -> [Span](https://docs.rs/struct.Span.html)

The span located at the invocation of the procedural macro, but with
local variables, labels, and `$crate` resolved at the definition site
of the macro. This is the same hygiene behavior as `macro_rules`.

[Source](https://docs.rs/proc-macro2/1.0.103/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/proc_macro2/lib.rs.html#405)#### pub fn [resolved_at](https://docs.rs#method.resolved_at)(&self, other: [Span](https://docs.rs/struct.Span.html)) -> [Span](https://docs.rs/struct.Span.html)

that resolves symbols as though it were at `other`.

[Source](https://docs.rs/proc-macro2/1.0.103/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/proc_macro2/lib.rs.html#411)#### pub fn [located_at](https://docs.rs#method.located_at)(&self, other: [Span](https://docs.rs/struct.Span.html)) -> [Span](https://docs.rs/struct.Span.html)

Creates a new span with the same name resolution behavior as `self` but
with the line/column information of `other`.

Convert `proc_macro2::Span` to `proc_macro::Span`.

This method is available when building with a nightly compiler, or when
building with rustc 1.29+ *without* semver exempt features.

[§](https://docs.rs#panics)Panics

Panics if called from outside of a procedural macro. Unlike
`proc_macro2::Span`, the `proc_macro::Span` type can only exist within
the context of a procedural macro invocation.

[Source](https://docs.rs/proc-macro2/1.0.103/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/proc_macro2/lib.rs.html#448)#### pub fn [byte_range](https://docs.rs#method.byte_range)(&self) -> [Range](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/ops/range/struct.Range.html)<[usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html)>

[Source](https://docs.rs/proc-macro2/1.0.103/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/proc_macro2/lib.rs.html#448)

#### pub fn [byte_range](https://docs.rs#method.byte_range)(&self) -> [Range](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/ops/range/struct.Range.html)<[usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html)>

Returns the span’s byte position range in the source file.

This method requires the `"span-locations"` feature to be enabled.

When executing in a procedural macro context, the returned range is only accurate if compiled with a nightly toolchain. The stable toolchain does not have this information available. When executing outside of a procedural macro, such as main.rs or build.rs, the byte range is always accurate regardless of toolchain.

[Source](https://docs.rs/proc-macro2/1.0.103/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/proc_macro2/lib.rs.html#463)#### pub fn [start](https://docs.rs#method.start)(&self) -> [LineColumn](https://docs.rs/proc-macro2/1.0.103/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/proc_macro2/location/struct.LineColumn.html)

[Source](https://docs.rs/proc-macro2/1.0.103/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/proc_macro2/lib.rs.html#463)

Get the starting line/column in the source file for this span.

This method requires the `"span-locations"` feature to be enabled.

When executing in a procedural macro context, the returned line/column are only meaningful if compiled with a nightly toolchain. The stable toolchain does not have this information available. When executing outside of a procedural macro, such as main.rs or build.rs, the line/column are always meaningful regardless of toolchain.

[Source](https://docs.rs/proc-macro2/1.0.103/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/proc_macro2/lib.rs.html#478)#### pub fn [end](https://docs.rs#method.end)(&self) -> [LineColumn](https://docs.rs/proc-macro2/1.0.103/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/proc_macro2/location/struct.LineColumn.html)

Get the ending line/column in the source file for this span.

This method requires the `"span-locations"` feature to be enabled.

When executing in a procedural macro context, the returned line/column are only meaningful if compiled with a nightly toolchain. The stable toolchain does not have this information available. When executing outside of a procedural macro, such as main.rs or build.rs, the line/column are always meaningful regardless of toolchain.

The path to the source file in which this span occurs, for display purposes.

This might not correspond to a valid file system path. It might be
remapped, or might be an artificial path such as `"<macro expansion>"`.

[Source](https://docs.rs/proc-macro2/1.0.103/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/proc_macro2/lib.rs.html#501)#### pub fn [local_file](https://docs.rs#method.local_file)(&self) -> [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[PathBuf](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/path/struct.PathBuf.html)>

[Source](https://docs.rs/proc-macro2/1.0.103/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/proc_macro2/lib.rs.html#501)

#### pub fn [local_file](https://docs.rs#method.local_file)(&self) -> [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[PathBuf](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/path/struct.PathBuf.html)>

The path to the source file in which this span occurs on disk.

This is the actual path on disk. It is unaffected by path remapping.

This path should not be embedded in the output of the macro; prefer
`file()` instead.

Create a new span encompassing `self` and `other`.

Returns `None` if `self` and `other` are from different files.

Warning: the underlying [ proc_macro::Span::join](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/proc_macro/struct.Span.html#method.join) method is
nightly-only. When called from within a procedural macro not using a
nightly compiler, this method will always return

`None`.[Source](https://docs.rs/proc-macro2/1.0.103/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/proc_macro2/lib.rs.html#532)#### pub fn [source_text](https://docs.rs#method.source_text)(&self) -> [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html)>

[Source](https://docs.rs/proc-macro2/1.0.103/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/proc_macro2/lib.rs.html#532)

#### pub fn [source_text](https://docs.rs#method.source_text)(&self) -> [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html)>

Returns the source text behind a span. This preserves the original source code, including spaces and comments. It only returns a result if the span corresponds to real source code.

Note: The observable result of a macro should only rely on the tokens and not on this source text. The result of this function is a best effort to be used for diagnostics only.

# RefineErr in unsynn - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/unsynn/^0.3/trait.RefineErr.html

```
pub trait RefineErr {
    // Required method
    fn
```
[refine_err](https://docs.rs#tymethod.refine_err)<T>(self) -> Self
       where Self: [Sized](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/marker/trait.Sized.html);
}## Expand description

Helper Trait for refining error type names. Every parser type in unsynn eventually tries to parse one of the fundamental types. When parsing fails then that fundamental type name is recorded as expected type name of the error. Often this is not desired, a user wants to know the type of parser that actually failed. Since we don’t want to keep a stack/vec of errors for simplicity and performance reasons we provide a way to register refined type names in errors. Note that this refinement should only be applied to leaves in the AST. Refining errors on composed types will lead to unexpected results.

## Required Methods[§](https://docs.rs#required-methods)

## Dyn Compatibility[§](https://docs.rs#dyn-compatibility)

This trait **is** [dyn compatible](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/reference/items/traits.html#dyn-compatibility).

*In older versions of Rust, dyn compatibility was called "object safety".*

# TokenCount in unsynn - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/unsynn/^0.3/trait.TokenCount.html

```
pub trait TokenCount {
    // Required method
    fn
```
[token_count](https://docs.rs#tymethod.token_count)(self) -> [usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html);
}## Expand description

We track the position of the error by counting tokens. This trait is implemented for
references to shadow counted `TokenIter`, and `usize`. The later allows to pass in a
position directly or use `usize::MAX` in case no position data is available (which will
make this error the be the final one when upgrading).

# AsDefault in unsynn - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/unsynn/^0.3/type.AsDefault.html

`pub type AsDefault<T> = `[Replace](https://docs.rs/type.Replace.html)<T, T>;## Expand description

Parse a `T` and replace it with its default value. This is a zero sized type.  It can be
used for no allocation replacement elements in a `Vec` since it has a optimization for
zero-sized-types where it wont allocate any memory but just act as counter then.

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

```
let mut token_iter = "..........".to_token_iter();
let parsed = <Vec<AsDefault<Dot>>>::parser(&mut token_iter).unwrap();
assert_eq!(parsed.len(), 10);
// Vec's ZST optimization at work:
assert_eq!(parsed.capacity(), usize::MAX);
assert_tokens_eq!(parsed, ". . . . . . . . . .");
```

# OrDefault in unsynn - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/unsynn/^0.3/type.OrDefault.html

## Expand description

Tries to parse a `T` or inserts a `D` when that fails.

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

```
let mut token_iter = "foo".to_token_iter();
let parsed = <OrDefault<u32, Question>>::parser(&mut token_iter).unwrap();
assert_tokens_eq!(parsed, "?");
```
Tries to parse a `T` or inserts a `D` when that fails.

```
let mut token_iter = "foo".to_token_iter();
let parsed = <OrDefault<u32, Question>>::parser(&mut token_iter).unwrap();
assert_tokens_eq!(parsed, "?");
```
